projectTitle: AIER: From Drupal 6 to a site the editors can run
project_haiku: The oldest economic research institute in the country was still publishing on Drupal 6, with two content types where one would do. We moved AIER to Drupal 7 and a shorter list of types their staff can actually edit.
project_footer_CTA: Sitting on a CMS your editors work around? We rebuilt AIER so the research could be filed once and found.
pageSummary:
The job

The American Institute for Economic Research, founded in 1933 in Great Barrington, publishes research, news, and teaching material. The site was Drupal 6. Articles and homepage "buckets" were separate nodes. Staff had a long path to put a paper on the front page, and the archive still had to stay findable.

What we built

The migration landed on Drupal 7 and six content types. Research articles absorbed the old article and bucket split, with "promote to front page," a taxonomy, related articles, and media on the node. News can point at an outside source and record the outbound click. Research keeps a twelve-month display cycle without dropping the document from the archive.

Outcomes

Editors file a paper once. The homepage, the mobile page, and the archive read from that same record.
